main_conditions: Metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer
expanded_sentences: The patient is a 47-year-old female diagnosed with metastatic hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, previously treated with endocrine therapy.
The patient experiences mild, ongoing cancer-related fatigue during systemic therapy, which began approximately 46 years and 8 months ago.
Initially diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast at the age of 45.
Liver lesions consistent with metastatic disease were identified at the age of 46 years and 6 months.

The patient's breast carcinoma is classified as Stage IV, with TNM staging of T3, N1, M1, indicating metastatic estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast carcinoma with liver involvement.
A core needle biopsy of the primary breast lesion confirmed invasive ductal breast carcinoma.
A core biopsy of a hepatic lesion confirmed metastatic breast carcinoma.
Tumor profiling identified a PIK3CA c.3140A>G mutation, which is relevant for targeted treatment selection.
The patient is currently receiving fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly and palbociclib 125 mg orally.
Magnetic resonance imaging was performed on 2026-02-18.
An elevated CA 15-3 level of 86.4 units per milliliter was noted at the progression assessment.
The patient's maternal aunt, who is alive, had a history of breast cancer diagnosed at the age of 52.
